rationale.complete: Round 1 plus round 1b (2026-10-04): all 29 periods rerun in 7 input configurations (bge and gte-modernbert, DQ5 dedupe, style residualization, shared goal vectors) and three native tests (G51 newcomer clock, G27 block switch, NE43 drive withdrawal) with dated predictions; per-period estimates written. Holdout not run; sub-day clocks remain round-2 work.
rationale.faithfulness: The core prediction (aging) fails in both embedding models and every configuration; #38 is the quench rival; #51 rejects mu = 0.5 aging; style residualization removes even #51's weak late slowing. Natives add no rejuvenation. Scorecard unchanged (A1 B1 C1 D0 E0 F1 G1 H0 I0).
rationale.usefulness: A model-robust settling picture (settle within days, then stationary; newcomers relax on their own clock) and a methods warning that now extends to step tests (fitted stationary nulls are too narrow at ordinary day boundaries). Reassurance, not a lever.

one_line: No aging: swarm content settles within about 4 active days of a kickoff, then decorrelates at an age-independent rate.

v2.claim: At day resolution swarm content does not age as strongly as mu = 0.5: in #51 mu = 0.5 aging is rejected (power >= 0.98), the random-effects aging slope over 10 long and medium goals is +0.02 +/- 0.02, and where age dependence appears (#38) it is a ~4-day kickoff relaxation with A_late <= 0; this holds in all 7 input configurations (both embedding models, dedupe, style residuals).
v2.scope: 29 non-holdout periods; powered only in #51 and for strong aging (mu ~ 1) in the long goals; weak sub-aging (mu <~ 0.3) not excluded

v2.adjudication_note: Different scope and power treatment: the coordinator scored the unscoped 'content does not age' with primary base, penalizing both the isotropic null (x0.7) and weak-aging power (x0.5); the blind rater scored a claim scoped to where the test has power, with secondary base. Ruling: secondary base (the headline null was chosen after data), scope the negative to mu >= 0.5 in #51 and strong aging elsewhere so the power rule is met, and count the calibrated null and the synthetic power as one design.
